notes:
- **Deleting a collection asks first.** The delete button on a collection now asks before it deletes, and says how many photographs are in it and that they stay in the catalog and on disk. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#collections).
- **Undo brings back a deleted collection.** **Edit > Undo** (`Cmd+Z`, `Ctrl+Z` on Windows) right after deleting a collection now brings it back with its name, look and photographs, and opens it again if it was open. Before, Undo took back the last edit on the photograph instead and the collection stayed gone. Undo and Redo go through deleted collections and photo edits in the order you made them. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#collections).
- **A restarted share opens on the first try.** After stopping a shared collection and serving it again, opening its address in a browser that had shown the share before could hang until you refreshed the page. The browser was reusing its connection to the stopped share, which no longer answered. Heeler now closes each connection after answering, and stopping a share closes every connection to it, so the first load reaches the new share and nothing is left open behind a stopped one.
- **A deleted collection leaves the ribbon.** Deleting the collection you had open left its photographs in the ribbon, as if it were still open. The library now goes back to the folder you were in before you opened the collection, or shows an empty ribbon if there was none.
- **A flushed or hidden folder stays gone.** Flushing or hiding the folder you were in opened it again straight away: the library went back to where you had been, which was that folder, and opening it added it back to the catalog, its photographs without the ratings, flags and keywords the flush had just cleared. The library now goes back to the folder above it, or to the last folder still in the list. A folder that already came back this way keeps the photographs it brought back, but not the ratings, flags and keywords the flush cleared; flush it again to remove them. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **The folder you clicked last is the one that shows.** Clicking a folder while a collection was still opening, or right after removing a photo from the open collection, could end with the collection on screen instead of the folder if the folder loaded first. This mostly happened with a catalog on a slow drive. The last click now always wins.
- **Stepping off a collection lets go of its photographs.** Clicking the empty part of the Collections list, with no folder open before the collection, deselected it but left its photographs in the ribbon under its name. The ribbon now empties, as it does when you delete the open collection. With a folder open before, it goes back to that folder as before.
